paragraphs: Here's what I see in this one, friend. God tells Elijah to go present himself to Ahab, and God adds that He will send rain (1 Kings 18:1). Elijah doesn't wait for the coast to clear. He walks toward the very king who has been hunting him, because the word came from the LORD. When God gives the order, God has already got the next part handled.

Now look at Obadiah, because I love this man. He is scared, and he says so out loud: "He will kill me!" (1 Kings 18:14). But he is also the man who hid a hundred prophets of the LORD and fed them (1 Kings 18:4). So Obadiah shows us that fearing the LORD can sit right next to a shaky stomach. Being scared doesn't cancel being faithful, friend, and I know a little about being scared in a dark place.

And then there's the standoff. Ahab calls Elijah the "troubler of Israel," and Elijah answers that the trouble is Ahab's, because he has "forsaken the commandments of the LORD" (1 Kings 18:17-18). The one who is troubling Israel is the one who walked away from God's word. So here's your takeaway, baker: stay close to what God has said, even when the whole room is against you. This story is NOT done, and the best part is still coming.
